Weekly context (gCaptain/Orbital Risk, Kelly): 15 attacks and piracy incidents worldwide in 7 days (+50% w/w, highest since mid-October), 7 strikes on 6 vessels in Gulf/Hormuz/Gulf of Oman; UKMTO period to 18 Nov 6 verified attacks (4 Strait, 2 wider Gulf); since the 17 Aug ceasefire expiry 6 vessel losses, 22 assisted, 31 continued; 2 seafarers missing, 13 injured (NAVIG8 MESSI 1 missing/11 injured under tow; TARA GAS abandoned). UOB via cappnotes: attacks running 'roughly one incident per day in November'; DTN: 19 tanker attacks in November through Thursday (UKMTO). Market reaction: Brent went from -0.83 at 9:30 EST to +0.59 at settle; the hit coincided with the Tasnim Qeshm 'missile' report (later re-attributed to munitions disposal). The IRGC's mine framing versus UKMTO's projectile/port-bow description is the same conflict as the 16-18 Nov hits; a port-bow strike with fire is consistent with a projectile, not a mine, but no authority has ruled. The IRGC did not claim the 20 Nov hit as an attack - the Araghchi interview the same evening implicitly keeps the 'unauthorised route / mine' narrative. Also in gate, Sat 21 Nov (Al Jazeera 09:30Z): IRGC claims an MQ-9 downed over Hormuz by a 'new air defence system' (58th of the war) and an MQ-1 over Qeshm (19th) - US military no immediate comment; unconfirmed, recorded as an M hit not a mine claim. Qeshm 20 Nov: Tasnim first reported a missile strike (ToI 6:19pm), then an official said the explosion and smoke were disposal of unexploded munitions (Reuters/ToI 7:15pm) - no strike confirmed.

Arab News headline: Bessent says the US will keep squeezing Iran's economy (not fetched). Two Cuba FAQs (1277, 1278) not standoff.

items.name: Trump at a White House press conference (Fri 20 Nov, ~12:57-14:05 EST, Vance and Rubio present): 'They want to make a deal, but they don't want to make a deal that's acceptable to me'; 'We want to make a real deal, not a fake deal... They've been bullshitting people for 51 years'; 'Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, ever' (invoking Bush's 'read my lips'); 'rumor' Iran is 'building a dirty bomb... We will not allow that'; oil 'almost down to $80', war's fuel-price impact 'far less than I thought', would 'absolutely' do the war again; Vance: blocking an Iranian bomb 'absolutely what we need to be doing'
items.headline: Trump: Iran wants to make a deal, but what it's offering is unacceptable / Trump insists Iran won't make an 'acceptable' deal as concerns grow about next steps
items.claim: Times of Israel liveblog (20 Nov 7:43pm, Jacob Magid): at a White House news conference Trump said 'They want to make a deal, but they don't want to make a deal that's acceptable to me' and 'Want to make a real deal, not a fake deal... They've been bullshitting people for 51 years'. AP (20 Nov 4:54pm): Trump repeated 'Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, ever'; he has oscillated between favouring an agreement and saying the US does not need a deal; a Middle Eastern diplomat said Gulf states seek a partial solution - lifting all constraints on Hormuz shipping in exchange for limited sanctions relief, paving the way for broader talks including the nuclear programme; mediating countries 'put little stock' in public statements and take closed-door talks seriously; a Navy-overseen coalition issued a new warning about ships that may be violating the blockade; Yacoubian (CSIS): neither side willing to jump back into all-out conflict, Iran may be hardening terms, depriving Trump of 'that face-saving off-ramp'; Singh: 'strategic patience'; Vaez: Tehran determined to show Washington cannot declare victory while keeping Iran under economic siege. ABC liveblog (12:57-2:05pm): Trump said oil was 'almost down to $80 a barrel' and he had expected $300, fuel prices rose 'far less than I thought', he would 'absolutely' do the war again; Vance called Iran 'the biggest state sponsor of terrorism'; ToI 8:37pm: 'rumor' that Iran is 'building a dirty bomb' - 'We will not allow that'. Al Jazeera 21 Nov: Vance declined to say whether he would have authorised the February strikes.
items.source: Times of Israel liveblog 20 Nov 7:43pm and 8:37pm; AP via news4jax 20 Nov 4:54pm; ABC News liveblog 20 Nov 12:57pm-2:05pm EST; Al Jazeera 21 Nov 09:30Z
items.note: Shift from Wednesday's 'we don't need a deal' and Thursday's 'not rushing' to an explicit 'we want a real deal' with a 'not acceptable to me' qualifier - the first time this month Trump has publicly confirmed Tehran is offering terms. No deadline, no mediator named, no strike order; paired the same day with the Witkoff/Kushner-Qatar 'no major progress' (T3 hit) and Araghchi's two-day plan (Iran-side T1 hit), so both sides are now publicly describing a deal they want on their own terms. The 'dirty bomb' rumour line and 'never have a nuclear weapon' keep the strike rationale alive alongside the deal talk. Oil comment: Trump framing the ~$80 WTI as a win is a political floor-reading for the O panel. Khanna/Ansari funding condition restated (Al Jazeera) - already recorded.

items.name: Araghchi interview with the Iran newspaper (Fri 20 Nov; Press TV 23:05Z, IRIB, newsquawk 21:36Z, Reuters 21 Nov): seven conditions 'must be implemented for the Strait of Hormuz to reopen' (end the war, lift sanctions and the naval blockade on southern ports among them); the two-day plan - US fulfils commitments day one, Iran reopens day two - is still on the table and Iran is willing to shorten the implementation window 'from two days to one day or two hours'; requires an explicit US declaration of readiness and tangible confidence-building measures; 400 kg of 60% HEU stays in Iran, a 'fair solution' is possible within a comprehensive package and mediators' proposals are 'worth examining'; 'no war, no peace' is undesirable but no deal that would 'hand victory to the other side'; messages exchanged via Qatar and Pakistan; 'We are people of diplomacy, and we still have hope in diplomacy'
items.headline: Iran FM outlines proposal to US, says seeks honorable agreement preventing return to war / Araghchi says Iran wants diplomacy to end war, Trump says terms unacceptable / Iran's IRGC downs US drone over Hormuz as efforts to end war remain stalled
items.claim: Press TV (20 Nov 23:05Z): Araghchi outlined a two-day plan, streamlined from an earlier seven-day framework - day one the US fulfils its required commitments, day two Iran reopens the Strait, paving the way for final talks; Tehran first requires an explicit US declaration of readiness and tangible confidence-building measures; 'If Iran's demands are met, the Strait will be reopened'; the 60% stockpile will not be exported, a fair formula can be reached within a comprehensive package, nuclear doctrine unchanged; any deal must be honourable, sustainable, prevent a return to war and avoid concessions the other side could portray as a political victory; mediators Qatar and Pakistan. Newsquawk (21:36Z, IRIB): the US must correct its position; Iran willing to reduce the Hormuz implementation time 'from two days to one day or two hours'; the 400 kg of 60% HEU stays for domestic needs; changing nuclear doctrine is disputed domestically and opposed by Russia and China; seven conditions before reopening; ready for dialogue if the US has implementation proposals. Reuters via Ariana (21 Nov 08:29 +04:30): Tehran wants 'an agreement that would ensure there was no further war', wants guarantees Washington is serious before going further, has discussed confidence-building measures with mediators; 'fair solution can be reached on the issue of nuclear material'; officials have floated diluting the stockpile under IAEA supervision; IAEA pre-June-2025 estimate 440.9 kg of 60%. Al Jazeera (21 Nov): he called the 'no war, no peace' situation undesirable but Iran would not accept a deal that would 'hand victory to the other side'.
items.source: Press TV 20 Nov 23:05Z; newsquawk 20 Nov 21:36 UTC (IRIB); Reuters via Ariana News 21 Nov 08:29 (+04:30); Al Jazeera 21 Nov 09:30Z
items.note: Most detailed Iranian deal text since the MOU collapse: a named sequence (US first, Hormuz second, nuclear inside a package), a compressible timetable ('one day or two hours'), a named mediator pair (Qatar and Pakistan - Pakistan re-enters after three runs absent; Oman not named by Araghchi though straits.live/Gulf News cite Omani channel), and an HEU red line with a dilution-under-IAEA formula floated by 'officials'. Contrast with the IRGC's Mohebbi 19 Nov ('battlefield or conditions'): same seven conditions, but the FM frames flexibility on timing and the stockpile. The 'seven conditions' list is still not published in full by any fetched page. Delivered the same evening Trump said Iran's offer is 'not acceptable to me' - the two statements are the public face of the terms being exchanged.

items.name: Mediator channel: Witkoff and Kushner met Qatari PM Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani and envoy Ali al-Thawadi in Berlin on Thu 19 Nov on a diplomatic resolution with Iran - Axios: 'no major progress has been made'; a low-level Iranian delegation met Qatari counterparts in Doha earlier in the week; straits.live 20 Nov: 'Washington and Tehran are exchanging terms through Qatari and Omani mediators. Nothing has been signed'
items.headline: No progress reported after Trump envoys meet with Qatari mediators to discuss Iran deal
items.claim: Times of Israel liveblog (20 Nov 9:09pm, citing Axios): US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani and his envoy Ali al-Thawadi in Berlin on Thursday to discuss a diplomatic resolution to the US conflict with Iran; Axios sources: 'no major progress has been made'; a low-level Iranian delegation met Qatari counterparts in Doha earlier that week. AP (20 Nov): Gulf Arab states are working through existing channels; a Middle Eastern diplomat described the partial-deal concept (Hormuz constraints lifted for limited sanctions relief, then broader talks). straits.live 20 Nov brief: Washington and Tehran exchanging terms through Qatari and Omani mediators, nothing signed. Press TV (Araghchi): messages pass through Qatar and Pakistan.
items.source: Times of Israel liveblog 20 Nov 9:09pm (Axios relay); AP via news4jax 20 Nov; straits.live 20 Nov brief; Press TV 20 Nov
items.note: late:true - meeting was Thu 19 Nov (pre-gate) but first reported 20 Nov evening and not in the 11-20 file. First dated Witkoff item in four runs and the first named US-mediator contact since the Islamabad MOU collapse: a real channel (Witkoff/Kushner-Qatar in Berlin, Iran-Qatar in Doha) with a negative result. Together with Trump's 'not acceptable to me' and Araghchi's 'two days to one day or two hours' it reads as terms being traded, not a deal forming. Axios itself not fetched (ToI relay).

items.name: Strike-planning plumbing, 20 Nov: CBS News (via ToI 3:05pm) - Israel and the US are weighing an attack on Iran 'in the near future', Netanyahu alarmed by Iran's missile rebuilding and moves to put missile and nuclear programmes underground, IDF on heightened alert for an Iranian first strike; Liberman (new Knesset FADC chair, Channel 12, ToI 9:44pm) - 'there is currently no urgency', no intelligence justifying a strike now, a strike now would be 'completely motivated by politics and not security concerns'; Qeshm blast ~18:19 Israel time first reported by Tasnim as a missile strike, then attributed by a Tasnim-cited official to disposal of unexploded munitions - no strike confirmed; Sat 21 Nov IRGC claims an MQ-9 downed over Hormuz (58th) and an MQ-1 over Qeshm (19th), no US comment
items.headline: Israel, US weighing attack on Iran in coming days - report / Liberman: There's no security justification for striking Iran now / Missile reportedly strikes Iran's Qeshm Island / Explosion on Qeshm Island said linked to disposal of unexploded munitions / Iran's IRGC downs US drone over Hormuz
items.claim: Times of Israel (20 Nov 3:05pm, Lazar Berman, citing CBS News unnamed sources): Israel and the US are weighing an attack on Iran in the near future; Netanyahu is reportedly alarmed by Iran's rebuilding of its ballistic missile programme and efforts to move missile and nuclear programmes underground; the report follows a string of similar dispatches that both countries have plans ready for an immediate attack; Israel's military is in heightened alert in case Iran attacks first. ToI (9:44pm): Liberman, days after being appointed Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee chair, told Channel 12 he does not know what Netanyahu is planning but 'there is currently no urgency', he sees no intelligence justifying a strike now, and a strike now would show 'it's completely motivated by politics and not security concerns'; Netanyahu has reportedly told aides renewed war with Iran is unavoidable and that a strike would require a unity government under him. ToI (6:19pm): Tasnim reports a missile hit Qeshm Island, cause unclear, no damage information; ToI/Reuters (7:15pm): Tasnim, citing an official, says the explosion and smoke were caused by disposal of unexploded munitions. Al Jazeera (21 Nov 09:30Z): the IRGC said a new air defence system shot down an MQ-9 over the Strait of Hormuz (IRIB; 58th since the war began) and later claimed an MQ-1 downed over Qeshm Island (19th); no immediate US military comment. AP: Iran widened attacks on Gulf neighbours in the past week after the 17 Nov US strike on the Qeshm IRGC missile site.
items.source: Times of Israel liveblog 20 Nov 3:05pm (CBS relay), 6:19pm, 7:15pm (Reuters/Tasnim), 9:44pm (Channel 12); Al Jazeera 21 Nov 09:30Z; AP via news4jax 20 Nov
items.note: No confirmed US or Israeli strike in gate: the Qeshm event resolved (per Tasnim) to munitions disposal within an hour, after briefly trading as a strike alongside the 214-26 tanker fire. The CBS 'coming days' report is the fourth strike-imminence dispatch in three days (NYT/Axios 4-7 day campaign, Channel 12 'backed out', Mako) and is now publicly contested inside Israel's own security establishment (Liberman, who chairs the oversight committee). The IRGC drone claims are the first claimed Iran-on-US kinetic events since the Sheikh Isa radar claim (17 Nov); if CENTCOM confirms an MQ-9 loss it is a hard-event candidate under the dashboard's confirmed-attack definition - at run time it is an Iranian claim only. Scorer: Israel pushing, Washington talking deal and keeping the strike option, Iran shooting at drones and tankers while offering a timetable.

items.name: Maritime regime, 20 Nov: UKMTO Warning 214-26 - outbound tanker hit by an unknown projectile 8 nm N of Khasab ~1500Z, fire, no casualties (IRGC: hit a mine); JMIC threat 'SEVERE', further deliberate attacks 'highly likely'; Orbital Risk: 15 attacks/piracy incidents in 7 days (+50%), 7 strikes on 6 vessels in Gulf/Hormuz/Gulf of Oman; UKMTO 7-day transits 115 out / 148 in (from 139/169); AP: Navy-overseen coalition issues new warning on ships possibly violating the blockade; hormuz.now 7d average rises to 6.9/day (8%), tankers 13/7d, visible tankers fall to 371/39 VLCC; straits.live 48 holding
items.headline: Another Tanker Hit in Strait of Hormuz as Maritime Attacks Surge Worldwide / Tanker catches fire after projectile strike near Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says
items.claim: gCaptain (20 Nov 09:43 PST): UKMTO Warning 214-26 - at about 1500 UTC an outbound tanker 8 nm north of Khasab, Oman, was struck on the port bow by an unknown projectile, the company security officer reported a fire onboard, no casualties, authorities investigating; Martin Kelly (Orbital Risk Intelligence): 15 attacks and piracy-related incidents in the past seven days, up 50% and the highest weekly total since mid-October, 7 strikes on 6 vessels in the Gulf/Hormuz/Gulf of Oman, 2 seafarers missing and 13 injured; UKMTO's latest period through 18 Nov: 6 verified attacks (4 Strait, 2 wider Gulf); since the ceasefire expired 17 Aug: 6 vessel losses, 22 assisted, 31 continued voyages; UKMTO 7-day transits 115 outbound / 148 inbound, down from 139/169, ~65% below pre-conflict; JMIC rates the threat 'SEVERE'. Reuters via Yahoo (17:04Z): UKMTO 'no casualties or environmental impact'; the IRGC said shortly afterward an oil tanker caught fire after hitting a mine while trying to transit near Khasab. AP (20 Nov): a Navy-overseen coalition issued a new warning about ships that may be violating the US blockade of Iranian ports; thousands of US troops remain off Iran's coast. hormuz.now (21:50Z): 48 crossings/7d, 8% of normal, last 24h 10 (7 in/3 out), tankers 13/7d, 371 tankers/39 VLCC visible. straits.live (21:00Z): 48 holding.
items.source: gCaptain 20 Nov 09:43 PST; Reuters via Yahoo 20 Nov 17:04Z; AP via news4jax 20 Nov; hormuz.now/traffic and /oil 20 Nov 21:50Z/21:34Z; straits.live 20 Nov brief 21:00Z
items.note: Regime unchanged and tightening on the kinetic side: a fifth Khasab-sequence hit in five days while AIS-visible crossings tick up (6.9/day) and the first MR-size tankers in five days transit - the hits are not stopping small/medium hulls, and the visible-tanker count falling (390 to 371) may mean departures via STS or AIS-dark rather than fewer ships. The blockade side is also hardening (new coalition warning on blockade violators). Araghchi's 'one day or two hours' reopening offer and the IRGC's mine framing of 214-26 sit on the same day. No CENTCOM/NAVCENT advisory text surfaced; no Aspides/EU escort item in gate.

items.name: Houthi-Saudi front escalates to ports, 20 Nov: Saudi-led coalition tells civilians to leave Hodeidah port then begins a 'targeted operation' (Malki: operational capabilities used for smuggling weapons and ballistic missiles), operations 'ongoing' in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz; Houthi spokesman Saree: Jeddah and all Saudi Red Sea ports are 'targets', shipping companies should 'immediately evacuate their ships from these ports', airlines should avoid Saudi airspace (Mecca/Medina excepted) which 'will be the scene of our operations in the coming hours', Shuqaiq power station threatened; Saudi Arabia intercepts multiple Houthi drones and missiles Friday; Marisks: 'significant' escalation
items.headline: Saudi coalition and Houthis exchange threats to bomb key ports / Saudis and Houthis continue exchanging threats
items.claim: Al Jazeera (20 Nov 14:48): the Saudi-led coalition urged civilians to evacuate areas of Hodeidah port 'for their safety', then said on X it had begun a 'targeted operation' against Houthi assets; spokesman Turki al-Malki said it targeted operational capabilities at Hodeidah port used for smuggling and transporting weapons and ballistic missiles, with operations ongoing in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz; Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree threatened to attack Saudi Arabia's Red Sea ports if Hodeidah were struck - Jeddah port and all Saudi Red Sea ports 'targets', shipping companies urged to 'immediately evacuate their ships from these ports', airlines to avoid Saudi airspace, a power station at Shuqaiq to be targeted; the Houthis struck a Riyadh tower the day before amid the heaviest air strikes since the conflict began and are advancing on Aden. ABC (2:31pm EST): maritime security firm Marisks called the escalation 'significant'. DTN (20 Nov): Saudi Arabia said it intercepted multiple Houthi drones and missiles Friday; the Houthis recently regained ground used to enforce an embargo on Saudi oil exports; attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure have accelerated. straits.live 20 Nov: Houthis ordered ships to leave Saudi Red Sea ports after the Hodeidah strike (gCaptain, MarineLink).
items.source: Al Jazeera 20 Nov 14:48; ABC News liveblog 20 Nov 2:31pm EST; DTN 20 Nov 8:42am CST; cappnotes 20 Nov; straits.live 20 Nov brief
items.note: Escalation of the Gulf-state front from Riyadh towers to Red Sea ports and oil-export routes: the Saudi east-west bypass (Yanbu/Jeddah side) that has carried Hormuz workaround barrels is now an explicitly named Houthi target set, with an evacuation order to shipping - relevant to the O panel's 'Middle East exports >80% of pre-war' framing. No strike on a Saudi port confirmed in gate; no Iranian strike on Gulf states in gate (Bahrain/Kuwait items are 15-18 Nov). Red Sea war-risk likely repriced but no figure surfaced.

items.name: Oil structure, Fri 20 Nov: Brent Jan settles 92.57 (+0.6%) after a morning low near 91.15, WTI Jan (new M1) 83.41 (+1.2%), Dec expires 83.98 (+0.9%); week -3.4% Brent / -5.2% WTI Dec, third weekly loss, ~-20% in November; Bloomberg: Brent prompt spread 'has weakened', 'geopolitics appears to be taking a back seat' (Ruecker), 'Without fresh escalation, the market remains biased lower' (Rasmussen), crude may struggle to fall further 'until we get solid evidence of a solution' (Hansen); IEA ~2 mb/d Q4 surplus; DTN: Mideast crude exports >80% of pre-war in October and climbing, UKMTO 19 tanker attacks in November through Thursday; UOB: 'roughly one incident per day'; Trump: oil 'almost down to $80', expected $300; energy sector -0.62%
items.headline: Oil Posts Third Weekly Loss Amid Surplus / Oil Prices Eye Third Weekly Drop as Surplus Signs Mount / Closing Look - Friday, November 20, 2026 / Brent Crude Price $92.57: 8 Days to OPEC+ 2027 Quota Call
items.claim: Bloomberg via Rigzone (20 Nov 4:25pm EST): Brent January settled +0.6% at 92.57, WTI January (most active) +1.2% at 83.41, WTI December (expiring) +0.9% at 83.98; Brent -3.4% on the week, third straight weekly loss, about one-fifth lower this month as Middle East supplies recovered and the US held off renewed strikes; Brent's prompt spread has weakened; Trump's 'not rushing' eased fears of renewed strikes; Energy Secretary Wright said Hormuz flows were at a record; US warplanes struck Qeshm this week and Tehran stepped up tanker attacks; Houthis continue to strike Riyadh; the US is widening its blockade of Iran; IEA forecasts a ~2 mb/d surplus this quarter, Goldman flags a 2027 glut; European gasoil fell on the week; US retail gasoline $3.69; Rasmussen: 'Without fresh escalation, the market remains biased lower, with weakness across commodities and fragile risk appetite'; Ruecker: 'geopolitics appears to be taking a back seat', 'we believe this pressure is likely to persist'; Hansen: crude may struggle to fall further 'until we get solid evidence of a solution'. DTN (20 Nov 8:42am CST): Brent Jan 91.15 (-0.83) and WTI Dec 82.63 (-0.58) at 9:30 EST; front-month Brent down more than 18% in November to a late-August range; Middle East crude exports >80% of pre-war in October and climbing in November, total outflows approaching February levels with Iranian exports nearly shut; UKMTO recorded 19 attacks on tankers in the Gulf/Gulf of Oman in November through Thursday; workarounds and a sizable surplus have reduced the perceived impact of disruptions. cappnotes (22:53Z): WTI +0.93% 83.98, Brent +0.64% 92.57 on 'Iran war worries and pre-holiday buying', energy -0.62%; UOB: attacks on Hormuz tankers 'running at roughly one incident per day in November'. financefeeds (21 Nov 07:00 GMT): Brent 92.57 -3.41% w/w (95.84 on 13 Nov), WTI Dec 83.98 -5.17%; IBTimes: the tanker fire 'revived shipping concerns'; OPEC+ 29 Nov 'the much more important test' (Rystad's Leon). ABC: Trump said oil was 'almost down to $80 a barrel' and he had expected $300.
items.source: Bloomberg via Rigzone 20 Nov 4:25pm EST; DTN 20 Nov 8:42am CST; cappnotes Closing Look 20 Nov 22:53Z; Reuters via financefeeds 21 Nov 07:00 GMT; ABC News liveblog 20 Nov
items.note: O-panel: a confirmed tanker hit, a Qeshm 'missile' scare, a 'real deal' press conference and a Saudi-Houthi ports exchange produced a +0.6% close and a -3.4% week - the market is pricing the surplus (IEA 2 mb/d) and the >80% export recovery over the kinetic tape, and Bloomberg's analysts say so in as many words ('back seat', 'biased lower'). Structure: the Jan/Feb prompt spread weakened Friday (no figure; Thu 2.54), so the one structural tightness signal that survived the $11 flat-price fall has started to give - M2 settle needed Monday to size it. Brent-WTI narrowed again (9.16 Jan/Jan). Energy equities underperformed (-0.62%) on an up-crude day. Dec WTI expiry at 83.98 above Jan 83.41 keeps a 57c prompt premium. Trump's '$80' framing is the political floor-reading. OPEC+ 29 Nov is the next scheduled O event; Jan Brent expiry 30 Nov.
